Find numeric values far from what other datasets report for the same species

Source: R/dataset_checks.R
dataset_check_outlier_by_species.Rd

Compares each numeric value in a dataset with the values other datasets in a compiled database report for the same taxon and trait, and lists those that differ by at least min_fold-fold. The question it answers is whether a value is plausible given everything else known about the species, which the allowed range in traits.yml cannot: a seed mass of 0.005 mg is in range for plants but not for an Angophora. This is a curation aid, not a test – species do vary – but a value 10, 100 or 1000 times what everyone else reports is most often a unit slip, a misplaced decimal point or a value mapped to the wrong trait.

dataset_check_outlier_by_species(
  database,
  dataset_ids = NULL,
  trait_names = NULL,
  min_fold = 10,
  min_other_datasets = 2,
  value_types = list(central = c("mean", "median", "mode", "raw"), minimum = "minimum",
    maximum = "maximum")
)

Arguments

database

Compiled database object, e.g. austraits

dataset_ids

dataset_id's to check. The default, NULL, checks every dataset in the database against the rest.

trait_names

Traits to check. The default, NULL, checks every numeric trait that cannot be negative.

min_fold

Values that differ from other_median by at least this factor, in either direction, are listed in records. The default, 10, catches unit slips while leaving most natural variation alone.

min_other_datasets

Minimum number of other datasets with values for the taxon and trait for a value to be compared. The default, 2, means a value is only flagged when it disagrees with the consensus of at least two other datasets, rather than with a single one that might be the one in error. Set it to 1 to also check taxa only one other dataset has measured.

value_types

List of groups of value_types to compare with each other; see Details. A value whose value_type is in no group is not checked.

Value

A list of two tibbles:

summary

One row per dataset, trait and group of value types with values that could be compared, so a dataset or trait missing from it had nothing to compare with. n_taxa and n_values count the taxa and values compared, n_flagged the values listed in records, and median_ratio is the median across taxa of each taxon's median ratio – far from 1 when the whole trait is shifted. Sorted with the largest shifts first.

records

The values at least min_fold from other_median, with ratio (value / other_median, so below 1 for a value lower than the others) and fold_difference (the larger of ratio and 1 / ratio), the range of the other datasets' values (other_min, other_max), how many values and datasets they comprise, and the record's details. Sorted with the largest fold_difference first.

Details

How values are compared. Each value is compared with other_median, the median, across the other datasets with values for that taxon and trait, of each dataset's own median. Every other dataset gets one vote however many values it holds, so a dataset of 30 individual measurements does not outvote three datasets of one mean each – which matters when the 30 values are the ones in error. The dataset being checked is never part of its own comparison. Values are compared as ratios, value / other_median, since errors such as unit slips are multiplicative and traits like seed mass vary over orders of magnitude, so only numeric traits that cannot be negative (allowed_values_min of 0 or more) are checked, and zeros are left out: a fold-difference is undefined for them. Traits that can be negative, such as water potentials and isotope ratios, are not checked.

Value types. Only values of compatible value_type are compared: value_types lists the groups, and a value is compared only with values in its own group. By default a minimum is compared only with other minima and a maximum only with other maxima – comparing a flora's maximum height with field means would flag every tall species – while mean, median, mode and raw values, which all estimate a typical value, are compared with one another. A value whose value_type is in no group, such as a bin, is not checked. To compare them all together, pass value_types = list(all = c("mean", "median", "mode", "raw", "minimum", "maximum")); to check means alone, value_types = list("mean").

Other attributes of a value, such as life_stage and entity_type, are not matched, and are returned so that a seedling measured against adults can be recognised as such.

Reading the output. A value with a ratio near 1000 or 0.001 – or 100 or 10 for traits such as lengths recorded in mm, cm or m – is worth checking first. A dataset whose values for a trait are all shifted, so that median_ratio in summary is far from 1 across many taxa, is more likely to have a unit or mapping error than one with a single flagged value. Traits that vary widely within a species, such as bark_thickness (with stem size) and plant_height (with age), produce the most flags that are not errors.

See also

dataset_check_outlier_by_genus() to compare with the rest of the genus, for taxa too few datasets have measured.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
outliers <- dataset_check_outlier_by_species(austraits, "Ooi_2007")
outliers$summary
outliers$records
} # }
